key_insight: JUCAL is a post-hoc calibration method that jointly calibrates aleatoric (label) and epistemic (model) uncertainty for classifier ensembles, producing better-balanced, more trustworthy predictive uncertainty than standard temperature-scaling or conformal approaches.
problem_solved: Existing calibration techniques treat prediction confidence as a single quantity and fail to balance how much uncertainty is attributed to inherent label noise versus model uncertainty, which can lead to misleading decisions, poor OOD detection, and suboptimal active learning or risk assessment.
method: Decompose an ensemble's predictive uncertainty into aleatoric (intra-model predictive spread) and epistemic (inter-model disagreement) components using ensemble outputs on a validation set.

Learn a post-hoc joint calibration mapping that adjusts both the overall predictive confidence and the relative proportions of aleatoric vs. epistemic uncertainty to match empirical frequencies/coverage on held-out data.
Design the calibration to be compatible with existing post-processing tools (e.g., temperature scaling, conformal methods) so it can be applied to trained ensembles without retraining models.
impact: By providing calibrated, well-balanced uncertainty decompositions, JUCAL improves decision-making in safety- and cost-sensitive applications (OOD detection, selective prediction, active learning) and increases trust in ensemble-based systems with minimal deployment cost.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: ensemble → decomposition into aleatoric & epistemic branches → joint calibration module → calibrated predictions
Before/after reliability diagrams showing calibration of total confidence and separate curves for aleatoric vs epistemic components
Stacked bar charts comparing proportion of aleatoric vs epistemic uncertainty across methods (uncalibrated, temperature scaling, conformal, JUCAL)
Scatter or ROC-style plot showing improved OOD detection/coverage vs. false alarm trade-off after JUCAL
paper_title: JUCAL: Jointly Calibrating Aleatoric and Epistemic Uncertainty in Classification Tasks
paper_authors: Jakob Heiss, Sören Lambrecht, Jakob Weissteiner, Hanna Wutte, Žan Žurič
